assumptions.condition: The directed graph \(\mathcal K\) is acyclic.
For every \(j\in V\), \(\Xi_j\) is a partition of \(\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal K}(j)\), with singleton blocks permitted.

standard.name: Blocked target-local edge colouring with a singleton-permitting variant

definitions.name: Singleton-permitting blocked-state class
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak S_p=\left\{A=(\mathcal K,\Xi):\mathcal K\text{ is an acyclic directed graph on }V,\ \Xi_j\text{ is a partition of }\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal K}(j)\text{ for every }j\in V\right\}.\]

definitions.name: Full blocked covariance model
definitions.construction: For \(E_0\in\mathfrak S_p\), let \(b_{E_0}=\sum_{j\in V}|\Pi^{E_0}_j|\), \(\Theta_{E_0}=\mathbb R^{b_{E_0}}\times(0,\infty)^p\), and \[\mathcal M(E_0)=\left\{(I_p-B_{E_0}(\beta_{E_0}))^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{E_0})(I_p-B_{E_0}(\beta_{E_0}))^{-\mathsf T}:(\beta_{E_0},\omega_{E_0})\in\Theta_{E_0}\right\}.\] The entry \((B_{E_0}(\beta_{E_0}))_{ji}\) equals \(\beta_{jB}\) for \(i\in B\in\Pi^{E_0}_j\), and all real block coefficients are admitted.

definitions.name: Observable rejection certificates
definitions.construction: For a rejected state \(J\), an ordered conditional-independence certificate chooses a topological order \(\pi_J\), a nonadjacent pair \(u,v\) with \(u\) preceding \(v\), and \(S=\operatorname{Pred}_{\pi_J}(v)\setminus\{u\}\), and evaluates \(f_{uvS}(\Sigma)=\det(\Sigma_{[u,S],[v,S]})\). A blocked-regression certificate chooses \(j\in V\) and distinct \(u,v\) in one block of \(\Pi^J_j\), puts \(P=\operatorname{pa}_{G_J}(j)\), and evaluates \(L_{j;u,v}(\Sigma)=(e_u-e_v)^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{adj}(\Sigma_{P,P})\Sigma_{P,j}\).

definitions.name: One-target binary-star library
definitions.construction: For \(E_0\in\mathfrak S_p\), choose \(z\in V\) and \(\mathcal A_z\subseteq\Pi^{E_0}_z\) with \(1\leq|\mathcal A_z|\leq2\), set \(A_z=\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal A_z}B\), \(B^{\star}=e_z\mathbf 1_{A_z}^{\mathsf T}\), and \[\Sigma^{\star}=(I_p+B^{\star})(I_p+B^{\star})^{\mathsf T}=I_p+e_z\mathbf 1_{A_z}^{\mathsf T}+\mathbf 1_{A_z}e_z^{\mathsf T}+|A_z|e_ze_z^{\mathsf T}.\] The set of all such covariances is \(\mathcal W_2(E_0)\).

definitions.name: Four-case binary-star router
definitions.construction: Order vertices, blocks, and pairs lexicographically. For \(\mathsf S(C)\neq\mathsf S(D)\), \(\mathsf{Route}(C,D)\) applies the first available rule: a skeleton mismatch activates the source block containing the differing arrow tail and returns the rejected ordered conditional-independence certificate; a collider mismatch activates the source block or two source blocks containing the collider parents and returns the rejected ordered conditional-independence certificate; a nonsingleton-family mismatch chooses crossing edge-support partition atoms, activates the source atom, and returns the rejected within-block regression certificate; an \(F\)-mismatch chooses a reversed \(x\to y\) with \(\mathcal N_x\neq\mathcal N_y\), selects a direction in which a block \(S\in\mathcal N_x\) is split by \(\Pi^E_y\), activates \(\{x\}\) and the first block \(T\in\Pi^E_y\) meeting but not containing \(S\), and returns the rejected regression difference between the first elements of \(S\cap T\) and \(S\setminus T\).

definitions.name: Partition-compatible singleton covered reversal
definitions.construction: For \(i\to j\) in \(G_{E_0}\), \(\operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}(E_0)\) is defined exactly when \(\operatorname{pa}_{G_{E_0}}(j)=\operatorname{pa}_{G_{E_0}}(i)\cup\{i\}\), \(\{i\}\in\Pi^{E_0}_j\), and \(\Pi^{E_0}_j\setminus\{\{i\}\}=\Pi^{E_0}_i\). It reverses \(i\to j\), sets \(\Pi'_j=\Pi^{E_0}_i\) and \(\Pi'_i=\Pi^{E_0}_i\cup\{\{j\}\}\), and leaves every other partition unchanged.

definitions.name: Legal-reversal component
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal R(E_0)=\{E'\in\mathfrak S_p:E'\text{ is reached from }E_0\text{ by a finite sequence of defined }\operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}\}.\]

definitions.name: Background-oriented consistent-extension enumerator
definitions.construction: Form the ordinary CPDAG of \(G\), orient every arrow in \(F(C)\), apply closure under the standard consistent-extension rules, and enumerate every acyclic extension \(K\) with the same unshielded colliders. For each extension emit the unique lift \(E_K=(K,\Pi^K)\) with \[\Pi^K_j=\mathcal N_j(C)\cup\left\{\{a\}:a\in\operatorname{pa}_K(j)\setminus\bigcup\mathcal N_j(C)\right\},\qquad j\in V.\] The emitted set is \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)\).

definitions.name: Off-model target-local block-constrained least-squares map
definitions.construction: Fix \(E_0\in\mathfrak S_p\), \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), and \(j\in V\). Put \(P_{E_0j}=\operatorname{pa}_{G_{E_0}}(j)\). Let \(A_{E_0j}\) have rows \(i\in P_{E_0j}\), columns \(B\in\Pi^{E_0}_j\), and entries \((A_{E_0j})_{iB}=\mathbf 1\{i\in B\}\). For a nonempty parent set define \(\Gamma_{E_0j}(\Sigma)=A_{E_0j}^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{P_{E_0j},P_{E_0j}}A_{E_0j}\), \(h_{E_0j}(\Sigma)=A_{E_0j}^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{P_{E_0j},j}\), and \(\beta_{E_0j}(\Sigma)=\Gamma_{E_0j}(\Sigma)^{-1}h_{E_0j}(\Sigma)\). Repeat each block coefficient on its member parents and put zero outside the parent set to obtain \(L_{E_0}(\Sigma)\); use a zero row for an empty parent set.

definitions.name: Global blocked-state BIC
definitions.construction: For \(E_0\in\mathfrak S_p\), set \(d_{E_0}=p+\sum_{j\in V}|\Pi^{E_0}_j|\). If \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), compute the attained statewise Gaussian likelihood using the target-local systems in \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\) and set \(\operatorname{BIC}_n(E_0)=-2\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal M(E_0)}\ell_n(\Sigma)+d_{E_0}\log n\). If \(S_n\notin\mathbb S^p_{++}\), set \(\operatorname{BIC}_n(E_0)=d_{E_0}\log n\). Let \(\widehat C_n\) be the minimizer under a fixed ordering of \(\mathfrak S_p\).

definitions.name: Component total-effect set
definitions.construction: For \(E_0\in\mathfrak S_p\), \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), and finite \(\mathcal Q\), define \(g_{E'}(\Sigma)=(((I_p-L_{E'}(\Sigma))^{-1})_{ya})_{(a,y)\in\mathcal Q}\) for each \(E'\in\mathcal R(E_0)\), and set \[\mathcal T_{E_0}(\Sigma)=\{g_{E'}(\Sigma):E'\in\mathcal R(E_0)\}.\]

definitions.name: Generic statistical exception set
definitions.construction: For \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), \(\mathcal E_C\) is the finite union, over \(D\in\mathfrak S_p\) with \(d_D\leq d_C\) and \(\mathcal M(D)\neq\mathcal M(C)\), of the polynomial pullbacks to \(\Theta_C\) of \(\mathcal M(C)\cap\mathcal M(D)\), together with the polynomial zero-gradient loci of the nonconstant coordinates reported by \(\mathcal T_C\).

definitions.name: Simultaneous component-effect confidence collection
definitions.construction: Select \(\widehat C_n\) by \(\texttt{def:global-bic}\). On \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), retain member labels, evaluate every rational map \(g_E(S_n)\) and its derivative, estimate its variance from the Gaussian covariance limit, and use Bonferroni critical value \(z_{1-\alpha/(2K)}\) for the \(K\) nonconstant labelled coordinates; assign exact singleton intervals to structurally zero coordinates. On \(S_n\notin\mathbb S^p_{++}\), assign \(\mathbb R\) to every coordinate. The resulting collection is \(\mathfrak I_{n,\alpha}(\widehat C_n)\).

definitions.name: Certificate Pareto-lower-bound handle
definitions.construction: Apply \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{opt}}\): restrict universal separator schemes to minimal crossing-partition and unequal-family reversal subinstances, translate active-block support into regression support rank, and use exact determinant divisibility and rational-height counting to lower-bound jointly the number of active blocks and the largest numerical height.

statements.statement:
Fix \(z\in V\) and \(A_z\subseteq V\setminus\{z\}\), and let \(\Sigma^{\star}=I_p+e_z\mathbf 1_{A_z}^{\mathsf T}+\mathbf 1_{A_z}e_z^{\mathsf T}+|A_z|e_ze_z^{\mathsf T}\). For \(j\in V\) and \(P\subseteq V\setminus\{j\}\), write \(r=r_j(P;\Sigma^{\star})\). If \(j=z\), then \(r_q=\mathbf 1\{q\in A_z\}\) for \(q\in P\). If \(j
eq z\) and either \(z
otin P\) or \(j
otin A_z\), then \(r=0\). If \(j\in A_z\) and \(z\in P\), put \(Q=P\setminus\{z\}\) and \(d=1+|A_z\setminus Q|\); then \(r_z=1/d\), \(r_q=-1/d\) for \(q\in A_z\cap Q\), \(r_q=0\) for \(q\in Q\setminus A_z\), and \(\det(\Sigma^{\star}_{P,P})=d\).
statements.justification: The exact regression table turns each combinatorial mismatch into an integer-valued observable certificate and controls every denominator.
statements.gap: SullivantTalaskaDraisma2010 expands covariance minors by trek systems, and DrtonRobevaWeihs2020 clears rational constraints through nested determinants; neither derives this one-target block-colour regression table.
statements.consumer: The four-case router uses the table to verify nonmembership without Gröbner-basis computation or numerical tolerance choices.

statements.statement: For all \(C,D\in\mathfrak S_p\) with \(\mathsf S(C)\neq\mathsf S(D)\), \(\mathsf{Route}(C,D)\) returns \(E\in\{C,D\}\), \(J\in\{C,D\}\setminus\{E\}\), \(z\in V\), and \(\mathcal A_z\subseteq\Pi^E_z\) with \(1\leq|\mathcal A_z|\leq2\). With every innovation variance equal to one, every block coefficient in \(E\) equal to one on \(\mathcal A_z\) and zero elsewhere, and \(A_z=\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal A_z}B\), the resulting covariance satisfies \[B^{\star}=e_z\mathbf 1_{A_z}^{\mathsf T},\qquad (B^{\star})^2=0,\qquad \Sigma^{\star}=(I_p+B^{\star})(I_p+B^{\star})^{\mathsf T}\in\mathcal M(E)\setminus\mathcal M(J).\] Every entry of \(\Sigma^{\star}\) is an integer in \(\{0,1,\ldots,p\}\), \(\det(\Sigma^{\star})=1\), and the router returns either an ordered certificate \(f_{uvS}(\Sigma^{\star})\) or a blocked-regression certificate \(L_{j;u,v}(\Sigma^{\star})\) whose value belongs to \(\{-2,-1,1,2\}\). Every recovered regression coefficient in the certificate has numerator in \(\{-1,0,1\}\) and reduced denominator at most \(p\), so all supplied numerical data have height at most \(B(p)=\lceil\log_2p\rceil\). The route uses polynomially many graph and rational-arithmetic operations in \(p\). For \(p=1\), the implication is vacuous.
statements.justification: This is the citation-independent necessity bridge: every inequivalent signature receives a sparse, bounded, exactly checkable observable witness.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Theorem 19 and Question 20, gives proper-blocked identifiability and an ideal-based equivalence test but no bounded witness theorem; SullivantTalaskaDraisma2010 and DrtonRobevaWeihs2020 give determinant-vanishing machinery without coefficient-colour height guarantees.
statements.consumer: A coloured-DAG solver can return a short certificate explaining why two fitted causal-community states are observationally inequivalent.

statements.statement:
For every \(C,D\in\mathfrak S_p\), if \(\mathsf S(C)
eq\mathsf S(D)\), then \(\mathcal W_2(C)
ot\subseteq\mathcal M(D)\) or \(\mathcal W_2(D)
ot\subseteq\mathcal M(C)\). Moreover, \[|\mathcal W_2(E_0)|\leq\sum_{j\in V}\left(|\Pi^{E_0}_j|+ inom{|\Pi^{E_0}_j|}{2}ight)\leq rac{p^2(p-1)}{2}.\]
statements.justification: The pointwise router induces a finite universal test dictionary whose size is explicit before any data are observed.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 decides equality using rational model constraints, whereas this result reduces inequality detection on the blocked class to finitely many binary stars.
statements.consumer: Exact-arithmetic regression tests can precompute the complete separating library for small or moderate labelled systems.

statements.statement: For all \(C,D\in\mathfrak S_p\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\); \(\mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D)\); and \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\). Every legal reversal preserves the full covariance image, including zero coefficients. If these conditions hold, then \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D)\), and a shortest path reverses every initially disagreeing arrow exactly once. Thus the signature is an exact recovery functional for the covariance-model component, not merely a sufficient invariant.
statements.justification: The theorem converts the observable separator into both a static criterion and a complete local transformation calculus.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Question 20, asks for graphical edge-coloured equivalence and Theorem 19 excludes singleton classes; Chickering1995, Theorem 2, permits every covered reversal and has no coefficient-partition legality condition.
statements.consumer: Singleton-permitting causal-community discovery can report the exact observational component rather than either forcing proper colours or claiming a unique DAG.

statements.statement: For every \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), \[\operatorname{Enum}(C)=\mathcal R(C)=\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}.\] Each consistent extension of the ordinary CPDAG with the background arrows \(F(C)\) has exactly one lifted partition, so the enumeration is duplicate-free and terminates after at most \(p!\) outputs. A shortest legal-reversal path from \(C\) to each emitted \(D\) has length \(\delta(C,D)\).
statements.justification: Exact equivalence becomes usable only when every compatible state and a shortest transformation certificate can be emitted without partition ambiguity.
statements.gap: WienobstLuttermannBannachLiskiewicz2023 gives linear-delay consistent-extension enumeration with background knowledge but does not prove the blocked-partition lift or its equality with a coefficient-coloured covariance component.
statements.consumer: The enumerated component supplies every member-labelled causal effect and every admissible singleton orientation for downstream analysis.

statements.statement: If every block of \(C\) is a singleton, then \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\varnothing\) for all \(j\in V\), and \(\mathcal R(C)\) is exactly the ordinary Markov-equivalence class of \(G\). If every nonempty block of \(C\) is nonsingleton, then \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\). The first reduction equals the Chickering1995 covered-reversal component, and the second recovers the BPEC structural-identifiability conclusion of BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 on the proper blocked subclass.
statements.justification: The endpoint reductions verify that the new component interpolates exactly between ordinary observational ambiguity and proper-blocked uniqueness.
statements.gap: Chickering1995 and BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 establish the two endpoints separately but do not characterize the singleton-permitting interpolation.
statements.consumer: The reductions provide exact regression tests for implementations and clarify when coefficient communities do or do not orient an arrow.

statements.statement: Fix \(p\), \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), and \(\theta_C\in\Theta_C\setminus\mathcal E_C\), and put \(\Sigma_0=\phi_C(\theta_C)\). Let \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}\) be independent \(N_p(0,\Sigma_0)\) observations, and let \(\widehat C_n\) minimize \(\operatorname{BIC}_n\) over \(\mathfrak S_p\) under the fixed tie rule. The set \(\mathcal E_C\) is a proper algebraic subset of \(\Theta_C\), and as \(n\to\infty\) with fixed \(p\), \[\Pr\{\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)=\mathcal R(C)\}\longrightarrow1.\] The result concerns the global criterion and makes no claim about greedy-search consistency.
statements.justification: Singleton blocks change the estimable structure from one state to an exact image quotient, so likelihood ties must be handled at the component level.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Section 6 and Discussion, derives decomposable BIC and reports GECS simulations but leaves consistency open; Haughton1988 treats a fixed finite collection of smooth models without this equality quotient and its algebraic intersections.
statements.consumer: A fixed-dimensional coloured-DAG analysis can consistently report the correct observational component despite exact likelihood ties among its members.

statements.statement: Under \(\texttt{thm:generic-bic-component-recovery}\), fix finite \(\mathcal Q\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). Then \(\mathcal T_{\widehat C_n}(S_n)\) converges in probability to \(\mathcal T_C(\Sigma_0)\) in Hausdorff distance. Retaining state labels before removing coincident numerical values, the confidence collection satisfies \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr\left\{\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)=\mathcal R(C)\text{ and every }g_E(\Sigma_0),\ E\in\mathcal R(C),\text{ belongs to its labelled interval in }\mathfrak I_{n,\alpha}(\widehat C_n)\right\}\geq1-\alpha.\] The conclusion permits duplicate effect values and singular joint effect covariance.
statements.justification: The observationally recovered object is a finite set of member-labelled causal effects, so inference must cover every component member.
statements.gap: NandyMaathuisRichardson2017 derives joint effect inference across ordinary equivalence classes, and StriederDrton2023 uses test inversion under equal variances; neither treats equality-constrained coefficient blocks after exact blocked-component selection.
statements.consumer: A causal-community analysis can report simultaneous uncertainty for all total effects compatible with its recovered singleton-permitting component.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{opt}}\), characterize the Pareto frontier of universal exact separator schemes for \(\mathfrak S_p\) in the two coordinates consisting of the maximum number of active target blocks and the maximum rational height. In particular, determine for which \(p\) the achieved pair \((2,\lceil\log_2p\rceil)\) can be improved in either coordinate without worsening the other, while every scheme must still separate every pair with unequal static signatures by an observable polynomial certificate.
statements.justification: The upper bound is operationally sharp only after the unavoidable support and arithmetic costs of universal separation are understood.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 supplies no witness-complexity notion, while general rational-identifiability arguments do not resolve minimum support or height on this blocked class.
statements.consumer: A lower frontier would certify whether any exact equivalence tester can use a smaller numerical alphabet or fewer activated communities than the binary-star library.

sampling_model.design: The identification kernel compares full positive-definite covariance images of centred linear Gaussian SEMs; the statistical rung uses independent Gaussian sampling and global BIC over the finite labelled state class.
sampling_model.units: Each observation is one independent realization of the \(p\)-variable system with known zero mean.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment in the structure-identification kernel; ordered pairs in \(\mathcal Q\) index downstream interventions and responses.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; every innovation variance is positive and otherwise unrestricted.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Target-local block-incidence regressions estimate one coefficient per parent block and one residual variance per target. The effect maps use the same constrained regressions before finite path summation. The inferential claims are fixed in \(p\), pointwise outside \(\mathcal E_C\), and conditional on global rather than greedy optimization.

estimand_functional: \(\mathcal R(C)=\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}\), certified on inequality by \(\mathsf{Route}(C,D)\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 19 proves structural identifiability within BPEC-DAGs, whose edge-colour classes all have size at least two, and Question 20 asks for a graphical characterization of edge-coloured model equivalence.
Theorem 2 transforms equivalent DAGs through exactly their distinct disagreeing edges, each reversed while covered.
Theorem 2.17 characterizes generic covariance-submatrix rank by trek separation and determinant expansions.
The paper explains classes of nested covariance constraints through restricted trek separation but gives no uniform arithmetic-height witness for coefficient-coloured model inequivalence.
Theorem 4.1 characterizes partial-homoscedastic model equivalence by ordinary Markov equivalence and fixed parent sets for vertices in nonsingleton variance blocks.
Theorem 4.4 characterizes existence and uniqueness of the MLE in a fixed compatibly coloured RDAG by linear independence of augmented sample vectors.
The paper gives linear-delay enumeration of ordinary Markov-equivalent DAGs and consistent extensions under background knowledge.
The paper extends Schwarz-type model-selection asymptotics to a finite collection of smoothly curved submodels of an exponential family.
The paper derives asymptotic inference for graph-indexed joint-intervention effects over an ordinary estimated Markov-equivalence class.
The paper constructs test-inversion confidence regions for total effects under equal error variances while accounting for structural uncertainty.

tldr: Target-local equality constraints among structural coefficients encode causal communities, but permitting singleton communities restores observational ambiguity. The headline result is a constructive necessity theorem: every mismatch of the proposed static signature is exposed by a unit-noise covariance generated from at most two coefficient-one blocks at one target, with integer entries bounded by \(p\) and an exact determinant or cleared-regression value in \(\{-2,-1,1,2\}\). This bounded separator yields covariance-model equality if and only if static-signature equality if and only if connectivity by legal singleton covered reversals, together with exact component enumeration. A qualified fixed-\(p\) rung then targets generic global-BIC recovery of the component and simultaneous pointwise inference for its member-labelled total-effect set.

project_justification.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 proves identifiability only when every blocked edge-colour class is nonsingleton and leaves graphical equivalence open. Its rational constraints and the determinant machinery of SullivantTalaskaDraisma2010 and DrtonRobevaWeihs2020 do not provide a uniformly small observable witness when singleton blocks are admitted.
project_justification.niche: The target-local blocked class has enough structure for every skeleton, collider, block-family, or unequal-family orientation mismatch to be routed to one sparse star calculation, while still containing ordinary Markov equivalence and the proper BPEC boundary as opposite special cases.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the four-case binary-star router and logarithmic numerical-height guarantee, lifts Chickering's disagreement-decreasing sequence to the exact legal blocked move graph, enumerates the resulting component, and attaches pointwise generic selection and effect-set inference without claiming uniformity at model intersections.

related_work: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 provides the writing and model exemplar: its Introduction moves from equality-constrained causal coefficients to causal communities, Theorem 19 proves proper BPEC identifiability, and Question 20 isolates general edge-coloured equivalence; the present strict advance is confined to target-local blocked colours with singleton blocks and adds bounded constructive separators. Chickering1995, Theorems 1 and 2, supplies the ordinary skeleton-collider criterion and the disagreement-decreasing covered-reversal induction; the new step is proving that equal blocked signatures force every selected move to be singleton and partition-compatible. SullivantTalaskaDraisma2010 supplies the determinant-expansion viewpoint, while DrtonRobevaWeihs2020 supplies the cleared rational-constraint analogue; both inform the certificate proof but are not claimed to be sharpened in their general graph classes. WuDrton2023 gives the nearest complete partition-restricted equivalence theorem for innovation variances, a different parameter restriction. MakamReichenbachSeigal2023 supplies the target-local pooled-regression likelihood construction. WienobstLuttermannBannachLiskiewicz2023 informs consistent-extension enumeration with background arrows. Haughton1988 informs the smooth finite-model BIC argument. NandyMaathuisRichardson2017 and StriederDrton2023 inform the simultaneous effect-set inference rung. Targeted searches through September 2026 found no paper occupying the bounded binary-star target-method pair or the stated singleton-permitting blocked equivalence criterion.
technical_internal_limitation: An independent exact-arithmetic implementation generated \(1\), \(3\), \(34\), \(1621\), and \(348631\) blocked states for \(p=1,2,3,4,5\). It verified every one of the \(1310886\) unequal-signature pairs at \(p=4\), including \(156\) unequal-family reversed-edge pairs, and all \(93380\) such reversed-family pairs at \(p=5\), using exact determinant or cleared-regression evaluation. These finite checks support but do not prove the all-\(p\) router. The statistical rung still requires full proofs of smooth embeddedness, properness of every exceptional locus, likelihood localization, and variance consistency.
honest_scope: Population equivalence allows zero coefficients and all positive innovation variances and makes no faithfulness assumption. The bounded separator and complete equivalence claims remain to be proved for all \(p\). The enumeration claim is finite and exact; no unverified linear-delay refinement is promised. Statistical conclusions are global-optimizer, fixed-\(p\), pointwise, and generic. Greedy GECS consistency, growing dimension, uniform inference near model intersections, cross-target edge-colour classes, constrained innovation variances, and cyclic graphs are outside scope.

literature_map: Boege, Kubjas, Misra, and Solus establish rational Markov properties and smooth geometry for coloured Gaussian DAGs, prove structural identifiability for proper blocked edge colourings in Theorem 19, and ask for graphical edge-coloured equivalence in Question 20. Their Introduction and Discussion supply the causal-community motivation and identify singleton or uncoloured edges as the unresolved boundary. Chickering proves that ordinary Markov-equivalent DAGs are connected by exactly the disagreeing covered-edge reversals; the changed step is to certify block legality throughout that sequence. Sullivant, Talaska, and Draisma characterize universal covariance-rank constraints by trek separation through cancellation-controlled determinant expansions. Drton, Robeva, and Weihs explain cleared rational constraints by nested determinants and restricted treks but do not control witness height. Wu and Drton solve the parallel equivalence problem for partially equal innovation variances. Makam, Reichenbach, and Seigal derive the compatible-colour pooled-regression likelihood geometry. Wienöbst and coauthors enumerate consistent extensions under background knowledge. Haughton supplies smooth finite-model information-criterion asymptotics; Nandy, Maathuis, and Richardson and Strieder and Drton supply adjacent effect-set inference constructions. Searches for later work citing the anchor, blocked edge-colour equivalence, singleton classes, and bounded rational covariance witnesses found no closer theorem subsuming the kernel.
novelty_justification: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 Theorem 19 excludes singleton edge-colour classes and proves uniqueness only within the proper blocked subclass; Question 20 leaves graphical equivalence open. On the target-local blocked class, the core introduces a deterministic separator using unit variances, at most two whole coefficient-one blocks at one target, integer covariance entries bounded by p, exact certificate values in {+/-1,+/-2}, and height ceil(log2 p). This constructive necessity theorem supports the complete static-signature and legal-reversal equivalence result. Exact checks through p=4 and all five-vertex reversed-family cases are recorded only as feasibility evidence.
